figures.finding: From the 2026 tax year, salaries, pensions and business profits are taxed on one scale: 9% to EUR 10,000, 20% to 20,000, 26% to 30,000, 34% to 40,000, 39% to 60,000 and 44% above, with lower rates for taxpayers with children and those under 30; the tax is then reduced by EUR 777 (no children), tapering by EUR 20 per 1,000 of pay above 12,000.
figures.applies: Income from 1 January 2026 (Law 5246/2025, FEK A' 198/11.11.2025, art. 3, replacing ITC art. 15(1)); tax reduction ITC art. 16.

figures.finding: The tax year is the calendar year; returns are filed electronically between 15 March and 15 July of the following year.

sources.said: No taxable years other than the calendar year are permitted.
The submission of the Greek income tax returns takes place from 15 March to 15 July for each tax year.

figures.finding: From 1 January 2025 an employee's social security contributions are 13.37% and the employer's 21.79% (35.16% in all), on pay up to EUR 7,761.94 a month from 1 January 2026.
figures.applies: Employees in the main fund (EFKA). Deloitte's Greece Highlights 2026 prints 13.77% for the employee against the 13.37% quoted here; e-EFKA's own rate page was not found, so the two readings stand.

sources.said: As of 1 January 2025, the social security contributions amount to 13.37% at the level of the employee and 21.79% at the level of the employer, i.e. 35.16% in total. The monthly social security contribution cap for the primary social security fund (EFKA) is set at EUR 7,761.94 from 1 January 2026.

figures.finding: The employer withholds income tax monthly: the annual tax on 14 times the monthly pay net of social security is computed on the scale and withheld at one-fourteenth a month (and on the bonuses).

sources.said: The WHT on salaries, wages, and pensions is calculated on the amount of monthly salary after being reduced by the employee’s share of social security contributions, multiplied by 14
The employer must withhold 1/14 of this amount each month from the employee’s salary.

figures.finding: Royalties paid to a non-resident are withheld at 20% (lower under treaties); no rule specific to a non-resident performer's fee was found.

figures.finding: VAT's standard rate is 24% (13% and 6% reduced; 30% lower on five islands).

sources.said: The VAT rate is 24%. The reduced rate on basic necessities is 13%. A super reduced rate of 6% is also available for certain items.

figures.finding: A taxable person whose supplies in the previous year were at most EUR 10,000 (net of VAT) may be exempt from filing and paying VAT, invoicing "without VAT - small-business exemption" and losing input-VAT deduction; an exempt person may opt into the normal regime.
figures.applies: Freelancers, 2026, per the VAT Code (Law 2859/2000) art. 39 as consolidated by TaxHeaven; AADE's own pages refuse this environment.

figures.finding: Royalties are income from capital, taxed separately at a flat 20%, and are withheld at 20% when paid to a resident individual; whether an author's own royalties instead count as business income on the scale is not settled here.
figures.applies: Resident individuals receiving royalties (Income Tax Code, Law 4172/2013, art. 40(3)); see the authors blocker for the business-income question.
